title: decimate
body:
## decimate

Reduces the polygon count of a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Decimate modifier in its default Collapse mode, keeping approximately ratio of the triangles. Use it to lighten heavy imports or remeshed surfaces for rendering or publication; geometric detail and sharp edges can be lost.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The Schemaxis default ratio 0.5 halves the triangles even when you only wanted to add the node; set 1 to keep everything.
- Do not use decimated geometry for measurements that need the original surface.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `decimate`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ratio` | Fraction of triangles to keep with Blender's Collapse decimation: 0.25 keeps about a quarter, 1 keeps all. Lower ratios lose more detail and can flatten sharp features. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `0.5` |
